description: One building's estimated devices from one Wi-Fi tick, as the browser receives them. Built by digital-twin (Rust) after each fresh `wifi-observations` tick and published on Redis `twin:devices:<buildingId>`. Parsed by socket (Rust), which routes it to that building's room only when `buildingId` matches the channel, then relays the received bytes as the `devices` event. Read by the frontend. Nothing is stored anywhere.

rules.buildingId: The building the tick came from; must equal the channel's building.
rules.tick: The collector snapshot these devices were placed from, Unix milliseconds. A browser drops devices older than 30 s: twin sends nothing for a building whose collector went quiet.
rules.devices: Every device placed this tick. Always present; empty clears the building.
rules.floor: Index of the floor, lowest first, as twin orders the building's levels.
rules.room: Id of the room the device stands in.
rules.x, y, z: Position in the twin's own metres; y is the floor's level, x and z lie on the floor.
rules.radius: One spread of the position, in metres along each axis.
rules.connected: False for someone passing who never joined the Wi-Fi.
rules.privacy: No token, MAC or any other id: nothing on a device follows a phone from one tick to the next.

cases.name: a connected phone and a passer-by on two floors
nobody placed, which clears the building

rejected.name: no buildingId
rejected.reason: socket routes on it; without it the room is unknown

rejected.name: no devices
rejected.reason: an empty list is how a building is cleared, so it is never left out

rejected.name: a device carrying a token
rejected.reason: a stable id would follow one phone through the building

rejected.name: a floor below zero
rejected.reason: a floor is an index into the building's levels
